paper.title: Algorithm 969: Computation of the incomplete gamma function for negative values of the argument

stack: Fortran 90 (TOMS 969: module IncgamNEG, with setprecision, cons, gammaError; driver testgamstar.f90)

claim.text: Shipped driver value gamma*(a,z) at a=-0.03, z=-0.03 (testgamstar.f90 DATA igams(11) = 0.98117651308252274; OutGammStar row '-.3000D-01 -.3000D-01 0.9811765130825D+00'), tol_abs 1e-9, fixed in the queue entry. Artifact-reference claim: the shipped expected value, not a value printed in the paper (the paper states relative accuracy about 1e-13 in this region).

attempt: Measured in the sandbox (tools/sandbox.sh), two passes, the same recipe (reports/gil2017-incgamneg-969/recipe.sh). Toolchain: gfortran 16.2.0 (conda-forge gcc 16.2.0-7) via micromamba into the sandbox scratch. Each pass copies the unpacked archive, builds the authors' Makefile in Fortran90/Drivers with make VPATH=../Src (gfortran -O, the Makefile's own flags; no source file is edited), and runs testgamstar, which writes testGammStar.dat. Row 11 (a=-0.3000D-01, z=-0.3000D-01) gives 0.9811765130825D+00 in both passes, agreeing with the shipped reference to 3.3e-16 relative (the driver's own ERR column) and with the registered value to about 2e-14 absolute, far inside tol_abs 1e-9. The driver prints 13 significant digits, so the recorded ours is that printed value; the registered claim is not edited.

original_attempt.reason: The authors' Makefile as shipped stops at once: 'No rule to make target setprecision.f90, needed by setprecision.o'. Its SRCS lists the sources that live in ../Src, not in Drivers, so nothing compiles without the VPATH build variable.
